It has also been said: the pronoun refers to the genitive noun, which is feminine beyond doubt. The nun was deleted from the end of the verb without analogy, likening it to the letters of prolongation in respect of the nasalization and quiescence and being among the augmenting letters. The analogical expectation was the return of the deleted waw after the meeting of two quiescent letters following the deletion of the nun, but they departed from analogy in this too, eager for lightening in what is frequently used. Yunus permitted deleting the nun from this verb also, as in his saying:

"If the mirror has not shown beauty, then the mirror has shown the forehead of a lion."

Sibawayh claims that this is a necessity of poetry.

Ibn Kathir read (hasanatun) with nominative, taking (takun) as complete, meaning: and if there is found or occurs a good deed. (Yudha'if-há) means: He multiplies it many times over, until He brings it, as has passed from Abu Hurayrah, to two thousand thousand good deeds, and it intends multiplicity, not limitation. The meaning is: He multiplies its reward, because multiplying the good deed itself, by making a single prayer into two prayers for instance, is inconceivable, though some verifiers have gone that way. What is in the hadith, that a date of charity is nurtured by the Merciful until it becomes like a mountain, is understood in this sense, since it is certain that it was eaten, and the possibility of restoring what no longer exists is remote; likewise the recording of its reward multiplied. This multiplication is not the multiplication in duration according to the Imam, because it is unending, and multiplying the unending is impossible. Rather the meaning is that He, exalted, multiplies it according to quantity: for example, he deserves ten units of reward for his obedience, so He makes it twenty units or thirty or more.

It has been said: it is the multiplication according to duration, in the sense that He, glory be to Him, does not cut off the reward of the good deed over endless durations, not that He multiplies its duration, majestic is His majesty, so that the hadith of the impossibility of multiplying the infinite would not arise. His saying, exalted:

﴿And gives from Himself a great reward﴾ is taken on this view as a conjunction explaining the bestowed reward, namely the increase in quantity following the explanation of the reward due, which is giving its like one after another to everlasting time. Calling that a reward is a metonymy of contiguity, because it follows the reward and is added to it.

On the first view, some took it as coming in the manner of explanatory conjunction, in the sense: He multiplies the reward of that good deed by giving what exceeds it from His bounty. They claimed that saying the reward is due is the doctrine of the Mu'tazilah, and it does not fit the doctrine of the Jama'ah. This is not so; for the Jama'ah also say there is entitlement, but by the requirement of the promise which is not broken, and thereby the promised reward is as if it were a right of the servant, just as it is also so by the requirement of generosity, as it has been said: the promise of the generous is a debt. Yes, taking the reward in the sense mentioned is not free from remoteness, and what motivates it is avoidance of repetition. The Imam also said: that multiplication is of the kind of the pleasures promised in Paradise, while this great reward which He gives from Himself is the pleasure attained at the vision and the absorption in love and knowledge.

In sum, that multiplication indicates corporeal felicities, and this reward indicates spiritual felicities. And there is no lack of beauty in this. (Ladun) means (inda), "at". Some distinguished between them, saying that (min ladun) is stronger in indicating nearness, and therefore one does not say (ladayya mal) except when it is present, unlike (inda), as you say: this saying is with me (inda) correct, and you do not say (ladayya) or (ladunni), as al-Zajjaj said. This was criticized on the ground that the use of (ladun) for other than place has become common, as in His saying, exalted: ﴿from Us, knowledge﴾. Unless what al-Zajjaj said is taken as the general case.

Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir, Ya'qub and Ibn Jubayr read (yudha''if-há) with doubling of the 'ayn. The preferred view among the lexicographers and al-Farisi is that the two have the same meaning. Abu 'Ubaydah said: (da'afa) requires many repetitions, and (da''afa) requires two times. This was rejected on the ground that it is the reverse of the language, since multiplication requires an increase in reward; when it is doubled, the form indicates multiplicity, so that requires repetition of the multiplication. What has preceded in the discussion is beneficial to you, so reflect.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 4, verse 41:

﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness, and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ The fa' here is faṣīḥah (an elliptical connective, indicating an implied condition). The word "kayfa" (how) may be in the nominative case, as the predicate of an omitted subject; or in the accusative case, governed by an omitted verb, being likened to a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative), as is the view of Sibawayh; or likened to a ẓarf (adverbial accusative of time), as is the view of al-Akhfash. The governing element of the adverbial accusative is the sense of the whole sentence, namely the awe and magnification derived from the interrogative or from the verb at the head of the clause, as established by the author of al-Durr al-Masun. The prepositional phrase is attached to what precedes it, meaning: if every small and great deed is recompensed for, then how will the state of these disbelievers, the Jews, the Christians and others, be? Or how will they conduct themselves? Or how will their condition be when We bring, on the Day of Resurrection, from every nation of the nations and every group of the groups a witness who testifies against them concerning the corrupt beliefs and vile deeds they held, and that witness is their prophet. ﴿And We bring you﴾, O Seal of the Prophets, ﴿against these﴾, a reference to the witnesses indicated by what has been mentioned, ﴿as a witness﴾ who bears witness to their truthfulness, since you know what they were sent with and you have gathered in your law all that they derived and established. It has also been said: [the reference is] to the deniers about whose state the question is asked, and he bears witness against them of disbelief and disobedience, in order to strengthen the testimony of their prophets, peace be upon them, or as they bear witness against their nations. It has also been said: [the reference is] to the believers, based on the saying of God Most High: ﴿That you may be witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾. When the one witnessed against is mentioned in the speech and "ʿalā" (against) is attached to him, there is no need to interpret testimony as carrying the meaning of recording.

Abu Dawud... [Transmitted by Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others, through various chains, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Messenger of God, may God's peace and blessings be upon him, said to me: 'Recite to me.' I said: 'O Messenger of God, shall I recite to you, when it was revealed to you?' He said: 'Yes, I love to hear it from someone other than myself.' So I recited Surat al-Nisa', until I reached this verse: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾ etc. He said: 'That is enough for now.' Then his eyes were streaming with tears."]

If this witness's eyes overflow with tears because of the terror of this statement and the magnitude of that situation, then by my life, what will the one witnessed against do? It is as though the Resurrection has already come down upon him.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 4, verse 42 (part 1 of 2):

﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish...﴾ This is a resumptive sentence (isti'naf) explaining their condition, the severity and dreadfulness of which has been alluded to. The tanwin on (idhin) (the "-in" ending of "that day") is, according to the correct view, a substitute (iwad) for the two preceding clauses. It was also said that it replaces the first clause alone, and it was also said that it replaces the last clause alone. The adverbial phrase (al-zarf) is connected to (yawaddu, "will wish"). To connect it to (shahid, "witness") is also possible, and the clause (yawaddu) is then a qualifying clause (sifah), with its returning pronoun omitted, meaning: "in it." This is far-fetched. The relative pronoun (al-mawsul, "those who") refers either to those who denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and expressing them by this description serves to censure them by what is in the scope of the relative clause (sillah), and to indicate the cause of the dreadful condition and the tremendous affair that befell them. Mentioning the Prophet (ﷺ) by the title of Messenger is to honour him and to increase the ugliness of the condition of those who denied him. Or the relative pronoun refers to the category of disbelievers in general, and those [who denied the Prophet] enter into their group by a primary entry. The word (al-Rasul, "the Messenger") here also refers to the category in general, and its nobility is increased by its including the Prophet (ﷺ) by a primary inclusion. The verb (ʿasaw, "disobeyed") is conjoined to (kafaru, "disbelieved") and is within the scope of the relative clause together with it. The meaning is their disobedience by means other than disbelief. This indicates that disbelievers are addressed with the subsidiary rulings (furu') with regard to being held accountable. Abu al-Baqa' said that it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in (kafaru), and the verb is then with "qad" implied. It was also said that it is a relative clause (silah) for another relative pronoun, meaning: "and those who disobeyed," so the report is about two categories: the disbelievers and the sinners. This is clear according to the view of those who permit the omission of the relative pronoun, such as al-Farra', but there is disagreement on this question. The meaning is: on that Day, because of its extreme severity and its doubled terror, those described above in the world will wish...

﴿...that the earth were levelled over them.﴾ It is either the object of (yawaddu), with (law) being a verbal particle (masdariyyah), meaning: they will wish to be buried, and the earth be levelled over them as they lie within it, or the earth be levelled over them like the dead. It was also said: they will wish that they had remained dust in their original state without being created, and they will wish that they and the earth were equal. It was also said: the beasts will become dust, and so they will wish for their state.

It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the meaning is: they will wish that the people of the gathering would walk over them, trampling them with their feet as they trample the earth. It was also said: they will wish that the earth would be exchanged for them, meaning that what is on it would be taken from them as a ransom. Or (law) is kept on its original meaning, and the object of (yawaddu) is omitted because the clause indicates it, as is the answer to (law) for the sake of making its clarity evident. The meaning is: they will wish for the levelling of the earth over them; [and] if the earth were levelled (law tusawwa), they would be delighted.

Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Yazid read (tusawwa) with the original form being (tatasawwa), so the second "ta'" was assimilated into the sin because of their proximity. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (tusawwa) by omitting the second "ta'," with imalah (vowel inclination). It is said: "sawwaytuhu fa-tasawwa" ("I levelled it, so it became levelled").

﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾ This is conjoined to (yawaddu), meaning that on that Day they will not conceal from Allah any statement, because they will be unable to conceal, since their limbs will testify against them regarding what they did. Or the meaning is that they will not conceal any of their deeds, but will confess them, and so they will be sent into the Fire by their own confession. They do not conceal because they know that concealment will not benefit them. They will say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ at some of the stations (of the Day of Judgement), as al-Hasan said.

It was also said: the waw is for the circumstantial clause (hal), meaning: they will wish to be buried in the earth while they do not conceal from Him any statement, and they will not lie to Him by saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾ This is because al-Hakim reported, and authenticated it, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that when they say that, Allah will seal their mouths, and their limbs will then testify against them, so they will wish that ﴿the earth were levelled over them﴾.

Making it a conjunction, with what follows it conjoined to (tusawwa), in the sense: they will wish that the earth were levelled over them and that they had not concealed the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his mission in the world, as is reported from 'Ata', is very far-fetched. Closer to this is conjoining it to the object of (yawaddu), in the sense: they will wish for the levelling of the earth over them and for the non-existence of their concealment, since they said: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.﴾

* * *

Furthermore, by way of allusion (ishara): ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾ by unveiling to you His secrets deposited in you during the journey toward Him, ﴿and to guide you to the ways (sunan) of those before you﴾, meaning their stations (maqamat), states (ahwal) and spiritual disciplines (riyadat). He alludes to those who have arrived (at Allah) before the addressees. It is also permissible that the allusion of "ways" refers to surrender (tafwid), submission (taslim) and contentment with what is decreed, for that is the habit (shanshanah) of the sincere ones (siddiqin) and the manner (nashnashah) of those who have arrived. ﴿And to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ from the sin of your existence when He annihilates you in Him. It is possible that "making clear" is an allusion to bringing (the seeker) to the unity of acts (tawhid al-af'al), guidance is an allusion to the unity of attributes (tawhid al-sifat), and repentance is an allusion to the unity of the Essence (tawhid al-dhat). ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of the degrees of your readiness (isti'dad), ﴿All-Wise﴾, and from His wisdom is that He bestows upon you according to your receptive capacities.

﴿And Allah desires to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ is a repetition of what came before, to indicate further concern with it, because it is the ultimate of ranks. ﴿But those who follow their appetites desire that you should deviate with a tremendous deviation﴾, meaning the fleeting pleasures (al-ladhdhat al-faniyah) which veil from arriving at the Presence (al-hadrah). ﴿Allah desires to lighten (the burden) for you﴾, meaning the burdens of servanthood in the station of witnessing, or the burdens of the self, by opening the door of enjoyment in worship after patience in it. ﴿And man was created weak﴾ in bearing the arrivals of the unseen and the onslaughts of witnessing, so he cannot bear that except through divine support. Or (he is weak) who cannot endure being veiled from his Beloved for a moment, nor can he be patient in seeking his object for an hour, because of the perfection of his longing and the increase of his passion.

Patience is praiseworthy in all situations except with You, for it is then blameworthy.

Al-Shibli, may Allah sanctify his secret, used to say: "My God, there is no rest with You, and no escape from You; the one sought for aid is to You."

﴿O you who believe﴾, true belief (al-iman al-haqiqi), ﴿do not consume﴾, that is, do not waste, ﴿your wealth﴾, which is what has come to you from the world of the unseen through acquisition by readiness (al-kasb al-isti'dadi), ﴿among yourselves by falsehood﴾, by spending it in other than its proper way and entrusting it to those who are not its people, ﴿except it be trade﴾, that is, except that the disposal be a disposal issuing ﴿from mutual consent among you﴾ and approval, cast into you from the world of inspiration (al-ilham); for that is permissible for you. ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ by heedlessness of them, for whoever is heedless of them is heedless of his Lord, and whoever is heedless of his Lord has perished. Or: do not kill yourselves, meaning your holy spirits (arwah qudsiyyah), by your engaging in what is unfitting, for engaging in what is unfitting prevents the spirit from flying in the world of witnessings and veils from it the lights of unveilings. ﴿Indeed Allah has been, in eternity of eternities, ﴾ to you ﴿Merciful﴾, and therefore He guided you to what He guided you. ﴿If you avoid the major sins of what you are forbidden﴾, and these, according to the gnostics (al-arifin), are: seeing one's servanthood in the vantage of Lordship; seeking recompense in service; the inclination of the self toward other than Him, from the Throne to the earth; resting in the station of miracles (karamat); and claiming lofty stations before arriving at them.

The greatest of the major sins is affirming a существование other than the existence of Allah, may He be exalted. ﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾, meaning We will wipe out from you your fluctuations (talawwunat) by the manifestation of the light of unity (tawhid), ﴿and We will admit you to a noble entrance﴾, which is the presence of the Unity of Being (hadrat 'ayn al-jam'). ﴿And do not wish for what Allah has given some of you in preference over others﴾, of perfections that follow from readinesses, for the attainment of one person's perfection by another is impossible if the latter is not prepared for it. For this reason He expressed it by "wishing": ﴿For men there is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning the individuals who have arrived, ﴿and for women there is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning those who are deficient and lacking, according to their readiness. ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾, that He may pour upon you what your receptivities require. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾, and among that is what you are of readiness, so He gives you what suits you.

﴿For each We have appointed heirs (mawali) of what the parents and close relatives leave behind﴾, meaning: for every people We have appointed as heirs (mawali) a share of readiness, by which they inherit from what their two parents left, namely the spirit and the heart; and the close relatives, who are the spiritual faculties (al-quwa al-ruhaniyyah). ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾, who are the murids (disciples), ﴿give them their share﴾ of the outpouring (fayd) according to their share of readiness. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, since every thing manifests one of His names.

﴿Men are in charge of women﴾, meaning the perfect ones, whose duty is to manage the deficient ones and to provide for them from their outpourings, ﴿by that in which Allah has made some of them excel others﴾ through readiness, ﴿and by what they spend from their wealth﴾ in the way of Allah, the Exalted, and the path to reaching Him, ﴿from their wealth﴾, meaning their faculties or their gnostic knowledge. ﴿So righteous women﴾, fit for the wayfaring, in the earlier sense, ﴿are devoutly obedient﴾, obedient to Allah, the Exalted, through the outward acts of worship, ﴿guarding in secret﴾, meaning guarding the heart from the defilement of blameworthy character traits; and perhaps this is an allusion to the inward acts of worship, ﴿what Allah has guarded﴾ for them of readiness. ﴿And those whose rebellion you fear﴾, their arrogance in submitting to what would benefit them, ﴿admonish them﴾ by mentioning the states of the righteous and their stations, for the self inclines, generally, toward what is praised for it. ﴿And forsake them in the beds﴾, meaning prevent the entry of the lights of your outpourings into the chambers of their hearts, so that they feel estranged; perhaps they will then return from that arrogance. ﴿And strike them﴾ with the staff of compulsion if admonition has not been effective in them. ﴿But if they obey you﴾ after that and return from arrogance and selfishness, ﴿then do not seek a means against them﴾ by imposing on them beyond their capacity, and contrary to what their readiness requires. ﴿Indeed Allah is ever Exalted, Great﴾, and despite this He has not burdened anyone beyond his capacity or contrary to what his readiness requires.

﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾, O guiding shaykhs, the perfected ones, ﴿between them﴾, meaning between the shaykh and the murid, ﴿then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family﴾, meaning send intermediaries from among the shaykhs and the wayfarers. ﴿If they desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them﴾, and the aspiration (himmah) of men uproots mountains.

It is possible that "men" is an allusion to the perfect intellects, and "women" an allusion to the deficient souls. There is no doubt that the intellect is the one in charge of managing the soul and guiding it to what reforms it, and by the two arbiters is meant then what mediates between the intellect and the soul from the spiritual faculties. ﴿And worship Allah﴾ by turning toward Him and passing away in Him. ﴿And do not associate with Him anything﴾ of what you suppose to be a thing when it is not a thing, since in truth there is no existence for other than Him, glorified is He. ﴿And to the two parents﴾, the spirit and the soul, from whose union the heart was born, ﴿be good﴾, ﴿goodness﴾: be receptive first from the former and turn in submission to Him; and purify the latter, and cleanse its two garments. ﴿And to the near of kin﴾, those who are related to you by original readiness and spiritual affinity, ﴿and orphans﴾, the ready ones cut off from the light of the Father, which is the spirit, through veiling, ﴿and the needy﴾, the workers who have no portion of gnostic knowledge, and therefore have stopped their journey; they are the ascetics. ﴿And the neighbour who is near﴾, the one close to your station in the path, ﴿and the neighbour who is distant﴾, the one far from your station, ﴿and the companion at your side﴾, the one who is in the very same station as you, ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, that is, the traveller who is estranged from the abode of the self and has not yet reached a station, ﴿and what your right hands possess﴾, of those who belong to you through love and will. It was also said: "the two parents" is an allusion to the shaykhs, and the disciple's goodness toward them is through obedience and submission to them and compliance with their commands, for they are the physicians of the hearts, the most knowing of the disease and its cure, and they do not treat except with what pleases Allah, the Exalted, even if its manner is hidden from the disciple.

And from here Junayd, may his secret be sanctified, said: "My Lord commanded me one thing, and al-Sirri (Sari al-Saqati) commanded me another, and I gave precedence to the command of al-Sirri over the command of my Lord. Everything I have found is from his blessings." He interpreted "the neighbour who is near of kin" as the speaking, knowing, loving, angelic soul (al-ruh al-nathiqa al-arifa al-ashiqa al-malakutiyya, al-malakut meaning the realm of the unseen dominion) which emerged from non-existence through the manifestation of the Eternal (al-qidam, the Pre-eternal) and was kindled from the light of pre-eternity (al-azal). It is the nearest of everything, and it is the neighbour of God Most High, dyed with His light. Its kindness is that you free it from the trial of nature (al-tabi'a), and sanctify its dwelling from the portions of human nature, so that it may fly on the wing of knowledge and longing toward the world of contemplation. "And the neighbour who is strange" (al-jar al-junub) refers to the form that carries the soul, and its kindness is that you wean its limbs from the one who has suckled the udder of desires. "And the companion at your side" (al-sahib bi'l-janb) is the heart, which accompanies you on the journey of the unseen. Its kindness is that you single it out from contingent things, and make it long for the beauty of the All-Merciful. It has been said that it is the commanding self (al-nafs al-ammara). In a report: "Your most hostile enemy is your self which is between your two sides." Its kindness is that you imprison it in the prison of servanthood, and burn it with the fires of love. He interpreted "the wayfarer" (ibn al-sabil) as the perfect saint (al-wali al-kamil), for he continually moves from the light of actions to the light of attributes, and from the light of attributes to the light of the Essence. Its kindness is to conceal his secret, and not to step outside the circle of his command.

Some of the knowers said: "If you wish, you may interpret 'those near of kin' as what is connected to the person of the abstract (al-mujarradat), 'the orphans' as the spiritual faculties (al-quwa al-ruhaniyya), 'the needy' as the psychic faculties (al-quwa al-nafsaniyya) of the outward senses and others, 'the neighbour who is near of kin' as the intellect (al-aql), 'the neighbour who is strange' as the estimative faculty (al-wahm), 'the companion at your side' as longing and will (al-shawq wa'l-irada), and 'the wayfarer' as thought (al-fikr), and 'those whom your right hands possess' as the acquired dispositions (al-malakat al-muktasaba), which are the sources of beautiful actions. The door of interpretation is very wide."

﴿Indeed God does not love one who is self-conceited﴾, who strives through spiritual travelling within himself, ﴿boastful﴾ of his states and stations, veiled by seeing them; ﴿those who are stingy﴾ toward themselves and toward those deserving, so they do not act upon their knowledge nor teach it; ﴿and who enjoin stinginess upon people﴾ by word or by state; ﴿and who conceal what God has given them of His bounty﴾, so they do not thank God for His blessing; or they conceal what they have been given of knowledge in the concealment of readiness and the darkness of potential, until it is as though it were non-existent. ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾, for the Truth, who veil the lights of unity with the darkness of multiplicity, ﴿a humiliating punishment﴾, which humiliates them in the abasement of their existence and the disgrace of their attributes. ﴿And those who spend their wealth﴾, that is, who display their perfections, ﴿to be seen by people﴾, showing off to people that these are theirs; ﴿and they do not believe in God﴾ with true belief, so that they would know that there is no perfection except His; ﴿nor in the Last Day﴾, that is, annihilation in Him, glory be to Him, so that they might appear before God, the One, the Subduer; ﴿and whoever has Satan﴾, the self and its faculties, ﴿as a companion, an evil companion he is﴾, because he misguides him from the Truth, like these people. ﴿And what would it have harmed them﴾, what would it have cost them, ﴿if they had believed in God and the Last Day﴾, affirming unity and annihilation in it, ﴿and spent of what God has provided them﴾, without seeing any perfection in themselves; ﴿and God is ever Knowing of them﴾, so He will reward them with subsistence after annihilation. ﴿Indeed God does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight﴾, the measure of what appears of dust motes; ﴿and if there is a good deed﴾, and it is not so unless it is for Him, and if it is for Him He multiplies it through the supporting divine aid, ﴿and gives from Himself a great reward﴾, which is the essential witnessing (al-shuhud al-dhati) or the knowledge bestowed directly from Him (al-ilm al-ladunni). ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, which is what presents itself to each person and appears to him in the form of his belief, thereby disclosing his state; ﴿and We bring you as a witness over these﴾, namely the Muhammadans, ﴿a witness﴾. Among the necessary consequences of bringing the Muhammadan Reality as a witness for the Muhammadans is their knowledge of God Most High at the transformation through all forms, so their witness in truth is none other than the Truth, glory be to Him. ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish﴾ because of their veiling, and because of their not following, ﴿that the earth were levelled over them﴾,

[Page 38]

so that their selves may be effaced, or that they may become plain, with no imprint of corrupt beliefs and destructive vices upon them. ﴿And they will not conceal from God a word﴾, that is, they will not be able to conceal a word from those imprints; and far-fetched it is: how could they hide any of them, when the mountains have become like carded wool?

An arrow that struck, and its shooter at Dhu Salam,
whoever is in Iraq, you have indeed sent your aim far away.

And God Most High guides to the Truth, and He guides to the right way.

[Page 38]

﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying﴾. This is a directive to purify the prayer, which is the head of worship, from the taints of turbidity, so that they combine sincerity in worshipping the Truth with the noble morals that are between them and creation, as mentioned earlier. By this the connection is achieved. It may also be said: since they were forbidden earlier from associating partners with Him, the Exalted, they are here forbidden from what leads to it from a direction they do not expect.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it sound (hasan), al-Nasa'i, and al-Hakim, who graded it authentic (sahih), narrated from Ali, may Allah honour his face, who said: «Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may Allah be pleased with him, prepared food for us, invited us, and gave us wine to drink. The wine took hold of us, the prayer time came, and they put me forward, and I recited: "Say: O disbelievers, I worship what you worship, and we worship what you worship," and so this was revealed.»

In the narration of Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir, from Ali, may Allah honour his face: «The leader of the people that day was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and the prayer was the Maghrib prayer, and that was when wine was still permitted.» The address is to the Companions. The opening of the statement with the two particles of calling and alerting (harfay al-nida' wa al-tanbih) is to emphasise the importance of the ruling. By "the prayer" the majority understand the specific form of worship, and by "approaching it" is meant performing it and engaging in it, though it forbids approaching it as an exaggeration. By "intoxication" is meant the established state that befalls one who drinks wine. Its root denotes blocking, as in "their eyes were intoxicated (sukkirat)," meaning they were blocked. The meaning is: do not pray in a state of intoxication until, before beginning, you know what you are saying before it, for by that it becomes clear that you will know what you will recite in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Jubayr that the meaning is: do not approach the prayer while you are drunk with drink, until you know what you recite in your prayer. Perhaps his intent is: until you are in a state where you know what you recite. Otherwise it would require that beginning the prayer precede the ultimate prohibition, and if that is intended, it returns to what was mentioned earlier. But there is in it unnecessary lengthening, and moreover the preference of "what you say" over "what you recite" would then be devoid of any motive.

It is reported from Ibn al-Musayyib, al-Dahhak, Ikrima, and al-Hasan that the prayer here means its places (mawadi'uha). It is then a metonymy (majaz) of mentioning the state while meaning the place, by the indication of His saying, later on: ﴿except as travellers passing through﴾, for that outwardly indicates it. Thus the verse is directed at forbidding the intoxicated from approaching the mosque, as a glorification of it.

In a report: «Keep your children and your insane away from your mosques.» But the outward sense of His saying: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾ rejects this.

It is reported from al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that he took the prayer to mean the specific form and also its places, out of consideration for both views. In that case the speech combines literal and metaphorical meanings, but we do not hold this.

It is reported from Ja'far, may Allah be pleased with him, and al-Dahhak, and it is one of two reports from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the intended intoxication is the intoxication of drowsiness and the overpowering of sleep. This is supported by what al-Bukhari narrated from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: «If one of you feels drowsy while praying, let him leave and sleep until he knows what he is saying.» A similar report is narrated from A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. But this is far-fetched, and even more distant is carrying it on both the intoxication of wine and the intoxication of sleep, because of what it contains of combining literal and metaphorical meanings, or the generality of metaphor without a clear indication of that. In any case, the prohibition's object is not the restricted (muqayyad) while the restriction remains permitted in its state. Rather it is the restriction together with the restricted remaining in its state, because the restriction is the locus of negation and prohibition in their speech, and because he is charged with the prayer and commanded to perform it, and the prohibition contradicts that. Yes, there is no obstacle to prohibiting the intoxicated from the prayer together with the absolute command, but its return is to this.

[Page 39]

The conclusion, as al-Shihab said, is that he is charged with it in every state, and the loss of his reason by his own act does not prevent his being charged. That is why his divorce and the like take effect. And if he were not commanded to perform it, he would not be obliged to repeat it if the intoxication covered its time. Al-Jassas stated this explicitly in (al-Ahkam) and elaborated it, end of quote.

Some claimed that the prohibition is against the prayer itself, but the intended meaning is the prayer in congregation with the Prophet ﷺ, out of glorifying him and honouring him, peace be upon him. It is not hidden that this is something neither transmission nor reason indicates, and the outward meaning and the occasion of revelation reject it.

It is reported that after the verse was revealed they did not drink wine during the times of prayer. When they had prayed the 'isha, they drank it, and so they would not wake except that the intoxication had left them and they knew what they were saying.

It is read as (sakara) with a fatha on the sin, the plural of (sakran), like (nadman) and (nadama).

Al-A'mash read (sukra) with a damma on the sin, as an adjective like (hubla), used as an adjective for a group, meaning: "while you are a group of intoxicated people." Al-Nakha'i read (sakra) with a fatha, and it is either a singular adjective describing a group as in the damma reading, or a broken plural according to Sibawayh and a collective noun according to others, since it is not one of the patterns of the plural. The first was preferred.

﴿Nor in a state of major impurity (junuban)﴾ is coordinated with His saying: ﴿while you are intoxicated﴾, for it falls under the accusative, as if it were said: "do not approach the prayer intoxicated or in major impurity." So said more than one scholar.

Al-Shihab, quoting al-Bahr, said: this is the ruling of the i'rab (grammatical parsing). As for the meaning, there is a difference between our saying "the people came intoxicated" (ja'a al-qawm sukara) and "they came while they were intoxicated" (ja'u wa hum sukara). The meaning of the first is: they came in that manner, while the second is: they came and they were in that state, with a fresh affirmation. Abd al-Qahir mentioned this. By "fresh affirmation" he means that it is established in itself regardless of the one it qualifies, and although it accompanies him, it indicates its establishment in itself, and it can precede it and continue. That is why al-Subki said in (al-Ashbah): if one says, "It is incumbent upon me before Allah, the Exalted, to perform i'tikaf fasting," he must fast for that vow without another cause, so i'tikaf with fasting in Ramadan does not suffice for him. But if he says, "and I am fasting," it suffices.

Perhaps the reason for the difference is that when the hal (circumstantial clause) is a sentence, it indicates simultaneity, while his actually being characterised by its content may or may not be the case, like: "Zayd came while the sun had risen." But a single-word hal is a description of a state. So if he says, "It is incumbent on me before Allah to perform i'tikaf while I am fasting," he has vowed that it coincides with fasting and has not vowed fasting itself, so it is valid in Ramadan. But if he says, "fasting," he has vowed fasting itself, so it is not valid for it. This matter was transmitted by al-Asnawi in (al-Tamhid), but he did not explain its reason, and we have not seen our scholars speak on it. End of his words.

He, may Allah have mercy on him, did not explain the secret of the difference between these two states in a way that clarifies what he mentioned in the matter. Al-Tibi, the scholar, explained its benefit, but he did not address this distinction. He said: its benefit, and knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted, is to indicate that approaching the prayer while intoxicated contradicts the state of the Muslims and of one who converses with the eternal Presence. The address with "you" (antum) indicates this, and for this reason He, glorified be He, joined it with His saying: ﴿until you know﴾ and so on.

Those in major impurity do not lack presence of heart, and for this reason they were granted dispensation on account of excuse. So reflect deeply.

The junub is one who has been struck by major impurity (janaba). In the eloquent language it is used equally for masculine and feminine, singular, dual, and plural, because it operates as a verbal noun, though it is not one, as some researchers said. Among the Arabs some make it dual and plural, saying: junuban, ajnab, and junub. Its derivation, as Abu al-Baqa' said, is from al-mujanaba, which is distancing.

﴿except as passers-by﴾ means: travellers through, ﴿a way﴾ means: a path, and the intended meaning is: except travellers. This is an exception of the emptied type (istithna' mufarragh) from the most general of states. Its place is the accusative as a hal from the pronoun in ﴿do not approach﴾, considering its restriction by the second state and not the first. The governing element within it is the meaning of the prohibition. That is: do not approach prayer in major impurity in any state, except in the state of being travellers, in the sense that in the state of travel the ruling of the prohibition ends. However, this is not by way of the negation covering all its forms, but by way of negating the generality in a general sense, without indicating the absence of the particularity of the negated part, nor the continuation of the particularity of the remaining part, nor the affirmation of its opposite, whether totally or partially. For the exception does not indicate that by its expression. Yes, it indicates the difference of the ruling of what follows from what precedes by a general allusion, which suffices in rhetorical contexts but not for establishing the legal rulings, for the basis of the matter in that is the textual proof, and it came after it by way of explanation. So said al-Mawla Shaykh al-Islam.

It was also said that it is a description of "junuban," with "illa" meaning "ghayr" (other than). This was objected to: such usage is valid only when the exception is impossible, and there is no impossibility here because the indefinite noun is general under negation. It was answered that this condition is in the case of description, as mentioned by Ibn al-Hajib, though the grammarians disagreed with him on it. Some preferred the descriptive reading here on the basis that a sentence under the assumption of exception gives restriction, and there is no restriction because the sick person comes as a difficulty against it, unlike on the assumption of description. Some claimed that the sentence gives that meaning absolutely, and that the sick person poses a difficulty, unless it is interpreted as you will come to know.

As for the one who takes the prayer to mean its places, he interprets crossing (al-'ubur) as passing through them, and it was permitted for the junub to cross the mosque. This is the view of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. Our well-known position is the prohibition of the junub from the mosque absolutely. Ali, may Allah honour his face, granted dispensation, as in the report of al-Tirmidhi from Abu Sa'id, on the basis of what Dirar ibn Surad explained when Ali ibn al-Mundhir asked him about its meaning. That Ali, may Allah honour his face, granted dispensation and then prohibited, is not established according to me, even if some transmitted it. Al-Jassas stated in (al-Ahkam) that entry is not permitted except if water or a path is in it. From al-Layth: a junub may not pass through unless his door opens onto the mosque, for it was reported that men from the Ansar had their doors opening onto the mosque, and major impurity would befall them, and they found no passage except through it, so they were granted dispensation in that.

﴿until you wash﴾ is a limit (ghaya) for the prohibition of approaching prayer in the state of major impurity. Perhaps placing the exception before it, as Shaykh al-Islam said, is to announce from the outset that the ruling of the prohibition in this surah is not absolute, as in the case of intoxication, arousing curiosity toward the explanation, and perhaps to increase its closeness in minds. It was also said: since His saying, glorified be He, ﴿until you wash﴾ had no place in the intended purpose, since the intended purpose is only the validity of prayer in major impurity, He delayed it and placed the exception before it. It would have been apparent not to mention it for this reason, but He mentioned it as an alert that major impurity is lifted only by washing. In the noble verse there is also a hint that the one praying should guard against what distracts him and occupies his heart, and purify his soul from what defiles it, because if purifying the body is obligatory, purifying the heart is more deserving. Or because if the place of prayer is protected from one who has a minor impurity, then the heart, which is the Throne of the Merciful, is more deserving of protection from an impure thought, which is clearly the more fitting.

﴿And if you are sick﴾ is a detailing of what was summarised in the exception, and an explanation of what is in the ruling of the excepted excuses. Limiting the earlier part to the exception of travel, while the rest share with it in the ruling of dispensation, indicates that it is the common excuse based on necessity, upon which the matter of dispensation depends. For this reason it was said that what is meant by other than "passers-by" is those not excused by a legal excuse, either by way of kinayah (implicit meaning) or by the textual indication and its implication.

وبِهَذا يَنْدَفِعُ الإيرادُ السّابِقُ عَلى الحَصْرِ، وإنَّما لَمْ يَقُلْ: "إلّا عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ أوْ مَرْضى فاقِدِي الماءَ حِسًّا أوْ حُكْمًا" لِما أنَّ ما في النَّظْمِ الكَرِيمِ أبْلَغُ وأوْكَدُ مِنهُ، لِما فِيهِ مِنَ الإجْمالِ والتَّفْصِيلِ ومَعْرِفَةِ تَفاضُلِ العُقُولِ والأفْهامِ.

والمُرادُ بِالمَرَضِ ما يَمْنَعُ مِنِ اسْتِعْمالِ الماءِ مُطْلَقًا، سَواءٌ كانَ بِتَعَذُّرِ الوُصُولِ إلَيْهِ أوْ بِتَعَذُّرِ اسْتِعْمالِهِ. وأخْرَجَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ أنَّهُ قالَ: "المَرِيضُ الَّذِي قَدْ أُرْخِصَ لَهُ في التَّيَمُّمِ الكَسِيرُ والجَرِيحُ، فَإذا أصابَتْهُ الجَنابَةُ لا يَحُلُّ جِراحَتَهُ إلّا جِراحَةً لا يُخْشى عَلَيْها".

وأخْرَجَ البَيْهَقِيُّ في (المَعْرِفَةِ) عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ مَرْفُوعًا: "إذا كانَتْ بِالرَّجُلِ الجِراحَةُ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ تَعالى أوِ القُرُوحُ أوِ الجُدَرِيُّ فَيَجْنَبُ فَيَخافُ إنِ اغْتَسَلَ أنْ يَمُوتَ فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ".

والَّذِي تَقَرَّرَ في الفُرُوعِ (الأحكام الفقهية المتفرعة):

[صفحة 41]

إنَّ المَرِيضَ الَّذِي يَخافُ إذا اسْتَعْمَلَ الماءَ أنْ يَشْتَدَّ مَرَضُهُ يَتَيَمَّمُ، ولا فَرْقَ بَيْنَ أنْ يَشْتَدَّ مَرَضُهُ بِالتَّحَرُّكِ كَالمَبْطُونِ (صاحب الداء في البطن)، أوْ بِالِاسْتِعْمالِ كَمَن بِهِ حَصْبَةٌ أوْ جُدَرِيٌّ. ولَمْ يَشْتَرِطْ أصْحابُنا خَوْفَ التَّلَفِ لِظاهِرِ النَّصِّ، وهو بِإطْلاقِهِ يُبِيحُ التَّيَمُّمَ لِكُلِّ مَرِيضٍ، إلّا أنَّ في بَعْضِ الآياتِ ما أخْرَجَ مَن لا يَشْتَدُّ مَرَضُهُ، وتَفْصِيلُ ذَلِكَ في كُتُبِ الفِقْهِ.

﴿أوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ﴾ عَطْفٌ عَلى ﴿مَرْضى﴾، أيْ: أوْ كُنْتُمْ عَلى سَفَرٍ ما، طالَ أوْ قَصُرَ. ولَعَلَّ اخْتِيارَ هَذا عَلى نَحْوِ "مُسافِرِينَ" لِأنَّهُ أوْضَحُ في المَقْصُودِ مِنهُ.

وفي (الهِدايَةِ): "ومَن لَمْ يَجِدِ الماءَ وهو مُسافِرٌ أوْ خارِجَ المِصْرِ، بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ المِصْرِ مِيلٌ أوْ أكْثَرُ، يَتَيَمَّمُ". والظّاهِرُ أنَّ حُكْمَ مَن هو خارِجَ المِصْرِ غَيْرَ مُسافِرٍ، كَما يَقْتَضِيهِ العَطْفُ، مَعْلُومٌ بِالقِياسِ لا بِالنَّصِّ. وإيرادُ المُسافِرِ صَرِيحًا مَعَ سَبْقِ ذِكْرِهِ بِطَرِيقِ الِاسْتِثْناءِ (الاستثناء: أي استثناؤه من الحكم المذكور قبله) لِبِناءِ الحُكْمِ الشَّرْعِيِّ عَلَيْهِ وبَيانِ كَيْفِيَّتِهِ، فَإنَّ الِاسْتِثْناءَ، كَما أشارَ إلَيْهِ شَيْخُ الإسْلامِ، بِمَعْزِلٍ عَنِ الدَّلالَةِ عَلى ثُبُوتِهِ، فَضْلًا عَنِ الدَّلالَةِ عَلى كَيْفِيَّتِهِ.

وقِيلَ: ذُكِرَ السَّفَرُ هُنا لِإلْحاقِ المَرَضِ بِهِ والتَّسْوِيَةِ بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَهُ، بِإلْحاقِ الواجِدِ بِالفاقِدِ بِجامِعِ العَجْزِ عَنِ الِاسْتِعْمالِ. وهَذِهِ الشَّرْطِيَّةُ ظاهِرَةٌ عَلى رَأْيِ مَن حَمَلَ الصَّلاةَ عَلى مَواضِعِها (أي المساجد)، وفَسَّرَ العُبُورَ بِالِاجْتِيازِ بِها، إذْ لَيْسَ فِيها حِينَئِذٍ ما يُتَوَهَّمُ مِنهُ شائِبَةُ التَّكْرارِ، بَلْ هي عِنْدَهُ بَيانُ حُكْمٍ آخَرَ لَمْ يُذْكَرْ قَبْلُ. وأُيِّدَ بِأنَّ القُرّاءَ كُلَّهُمُ اسْتَحَبُّوا الوَقْفَ عِنْدَ قَوْلِهِ سُبْحانَهُ: ﴿حَتّى تَغْتَسِلُوا﴾، ويَبْتَدِئُونَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وإنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ إلَخْ. بَلِ التَّعْبِيرُ بِالقُرْبِ يُومِئُ إلى حَمْلِ الصَّلاةِ عَلى ذَلِكَ، لِأنَّ حَقِيقَةَ القُرْبِ والبُعْدِ في المَكانِ. وكَذا التَّعْبِيرُ بِـ﴿عابِرِي سَبِيلٍ﴾ هُناكَ وبِـ﴿عَلى سَفَرٍ﴾ هُنا فِيهِ إيماءٌ إلى الفَرْقِ بَيْنَ ما هُنا وما هُناكَ، إلّا أنَّ الكَثِيرَ عَلى خِلافِهِ. وإنَّما قُدِّمَ المَرَضُ عَلى السَّفَرِ لِلْإيذانِ بِأصالَتِهِ واسْتِقْلالِهِ بِأحْكامٍ لا تُوجَدُ في غَيْرِهِ. وقِيلَ: لِأنَّهُ سَبَبُ النُّزُولِ، فَقَدْ أخْرَجَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ عَنْ إبْراهِيمَ النَّخَعِيِّ قالَ: "نالَ أصْحابَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ جِراحَةٌ فَفَشَتْ فِيهِمْ، ثُمَّ ابْتُلُوا بِالجَنابَةِ، فَشَكَوْا ذَلِكَ إلى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَنَزَلَتْ: ﴿وإنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى﴾ الآيَةَ كُلَّها".

وهَذا خِلافُ ما عَلَيْهِ الجُمْهُورُ، حَيْثُ رَوَوْا أنَّ نُزُولَها كانَ في غَزْوَةِ المُرَيْسِيعِ: "حِينَ عَرَّسَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ لَيْلَةً، فَسَقَطَتْ عَنْ عائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْها قِلادَةٌ لِأسْماءَ، فَلَمّا ارْتَحَلُوا ذَكَرَتْ ذَلِكَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَبَعَثَ رَجُلَيْنِ في طَلَبِها، فَنَزَلُوا يَنْتَظِرُونَهُما، فَأصْبَحُوا ولَيْسَ مَعَهُمْ ماءٌ، فَأغْلَظَ أبُو بَكْرٍ عَلى عائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْها وقالَ: حَبَسْتِ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ والمُسْلِمِينَ عَلى غَيْرِ ماءٍ، فَنَزَلَتْ. فَلَمّا صَلَّوْا بِالتَّيَمُّمِ جاءَ أُسَيْدُ بْنُ الحُضَيْرِ إلى مَضْرِبِ عائِشَةَ فَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ: ما أكْثَرَ بَرَكَتَكُمْ يا آلَ أبِي بَكْرٍ!" وفي رِوايَةٍ: "يَرْحَمُكِ اللَّهُ تَعالى يا عائِشَةُ، ما نَزَلَ بِكِ أمْرٌ تَكْرَهِينَهُ إلّا جَعَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى فِيهِ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ فَرَجًا".

وهَذا يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ سَبَبَ النُّزُولِ كانَ فَقْدَ الماءِ في السَّفَرِ، وهو ظاهِرٌ.

﴿أوْ جاءَ أحَدٌ مِنكم مِنَ الغائِطِ﴾. والغائِطُ هو المَكانُ المُنْخَفِضُ. وقَرَأ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: "أوْ جاءَ الغَيْطَ"، بِفَتْحِ الغَيْنِ وسُكُونِ الياءِ، وهو في رَأْيٍ مَصْدَرُ "يَغُوطُ"، وكانَ القِياسُ "غَوْطًا" فَقُلِبَتِ الواوُ ياءً، وسُكِّنَتْ، وانْفَتَحَ ما قَبْلَها لِخِفَّتِها. ولَعَلَّ الأوْلى ما قِيلَ: إنَّهُ تَخْفِيفُ "غَيِّطٍ"، كَـ"هَيْنٍ" و"هَيِّنٍ"، والغَيْطُ هو الغائِطُ. والمَجِيءُ مِنهُ كِنايَةٌ عَنِ الحَدَثِ (ما يوجب الوضوء أو الغسل)، لِأنَّ العادَةَ أنَّ مَن يُرِيدُهُ يَذْهَبُ إلَيْهِ لِيُوارِيَ شَخْصَهُ عَنْ أعْيُنِ النّاسِ.

وفي ذِكْرِ "أحَدٍ" فِيهِ دُونَ غَيْرِهِ إيماءٌ إلى أنَّ الإنْسانَ يَنْفَرِدُ عِنْدَ قَضاءِ الحاجَةِ، كَما هو دَأْبُهُ وأدَبُهُ. وقِيلَ: إنَّما ذُكِرَ وأُسْنِدَ المَجِيءُ إلَيْهِ دُونَ المُخاطَبِينَ تَفادِيًا عَنِ التَّصْرِيحِ بِنِسْبَتِهِمْ إلى ما يُسْتَحى مِنهُ، أوْ يُسْتَهْجَنُ التَّصْرِيحُ بِهِ. والفِعْلُ عَطْفٌ عَلى "كُنْتُمْ"، والجارُّ الأوَّلُ (مِنكم) مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِمَحْذُوفٍ وقَعَ صِفَةً لِلنَّكِرَةِ قَبْلَهُ، والثّانِي (مِنَ الغائِطِ) مُتَعَلِّقٌ بِالفِعْلِ، أيْ: وإنْ جاءَ أحَدٌ كائِنٌ مِنكم مِنَ الغائِطِ.

﴿أوْ لامَسْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾. يُرِيدُ سُبْحانَهُ: "أوْ جامَعْتُمُ النِّساءَ"، إلّا أنَّهُ

[صفحة 42]

كَنّى بِالمُلامَسَةِ عَنِ الجِماعِ، لِأنَّهُ مِمّا يُسْتَهْجَنُ التَّصْرِيحُ بِهِ أوْ يُسْتَحى مِنهُ. وإلى ذَلِكَ ذَهَبَ عَلِيٌّ كَرَّمَ اللَّهُ وجْهَهُ، وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُما، والحَسَنُ، فَيَكُونُ إشارَةً إلى الحَدَثِ الأكْبَرِ (الجنابة)، كَما أنَّ الأوَّلَ إشارَةٌ إلى الحَدَثِ الأصْغَرِ.

وعَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ والنَّخَعِيِّ والشَّعْبِيِّ أنَّ المُرادَ بِالمُلامَسَةِ ما دُونَ الجِماعِ، أيْ: ماسَسْتُمْ بَشْرَتَهُنَّ بِبَشْرَتِكُمْ. وبِهِ اسْتَدَلَّ الشّافِعِيُّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ عَلى أنَّ اللَّمْسَ يَنْقُضُ الوُضُوءَ (الطهارة الصغرى)، وبِهِ قالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ والأوْزاعِيُّ. وقالَ مالِكٌ واللَّيْثُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ، وأحْمَدُ في إحْدى الرِّواياتِ عَنْهُ: إنْ كانَ اللَّمْسُ بِشَهْوَةٍ نَقَضَ، وإلّا فَلا. وذَهَبَ أبُو حَنِيفَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ إلى أنَّهُ لا يَنْتَقِضُ الوُضُوءُ بِالمَسِّ ولَوْ بِشَهْوَةٍ، وقِيلَ: ما لَمْ يُحْدِثِ الِانْتِشارَ.

واخْتَلَفَ قَوْلُ الشّافِعِيِّ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ في لَمْسِ المَحارِمِ كالأُمِّ والبِنْتِ والأُخْتِ، وفي لَمْسِ الأجْنَبِيَّةِ الصَّغِيرَةِ. وأصَحُّ القَوْلَيْنِ: أنَّهُ لا يَنْقُضُ، كَلَمْسِ نَحْوِ السِّنِّ والظُّفْرِ والشَّعَرِ. ويَنْتَقِضُ عِنْدَهُ وُضُوءُ المَلْمُوسَةِ كَاللّامِسِ في الأظْهَرِ، لِاشْتِراكِهِما في مَظِنَّةِ اللَّذَّةِ، كَالمُشْتَرِكَيْنِ في الجِماعِ. وإنَّما لَمْ يَنْتَقِضْ وُضُوءُ المَلْمُوسِ فَرْجُهُ عَلى مَذْهَبِهِ، لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يُوجَدْ مِنهُ مَسٌّ لِمَظِنَّةِ لَذَّةٍ أصْلًا، بِخِلافِهِ هُنا.

ودَلِيلُ القَوْلِ بِعَدَمِ نَقْضِ وُضُوءِ المَلْمُوسِ حَدِيثُ عائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْها أنَّها وضَعَتْ يَدَها عَلى قَدَمَيْهِ ﷺ وهو ساجِدٌ. وَوَجْهُ اسْتِدْلالِهِ بِما في الآيَةِ عَلى ما اسْتَدَلَّ عَلَيْهِ: أنَّ حَمْلَ اللَّفْظِ عَلى الحَقِيقَةِ (المعنى الأصلي الظاهر) هو الراجِحُ، لا سِيَّما في قِراءَةِ حَمْزَةَ والكِسائِيِّ: "أوْ لَمَسْتُمُ"، إذْ لَمْ يَشْتَهِرِ اللَّمْسُ في الجِماعِ كالمُلامَسَةِ. ورَجَّحَ بَعْضُهُمُ الحَمْلَ عَلى الجِماعِ في القِراءَتَيْنِ، تَرْجِيحًا لِلْمَجازِ (المعنى المنقول بالاستعمال) والمَشْهُورِ، وعَمَلًا بِهِما إذْ لا مُنافاةَ بَيْنَهُما، وهو الأوْفَقُ بِمَذْهَبِنا.

وقالَ بَعْضُ المُحَقِّقِينَ: إنَّ المُتَّجَهَ أنَّ المُلامَسَةَ حَقِيقَةٌ في تَماسِّ البَدَنَيْنِ بِشَيْءٍ مِن أجْزائِهِما مِن غَيْرِ تَقْيِيدٍ بِاليَدِ، وعَلى هَذا فالجِماعُ مِن أفْرادِ مُسَمّى الحَقِيقَةِ، فَيَتَناوَلُهُ اللَّفْظُ حَقِيقَةً، وإنَّما يَكُونُ مَجازًا لَوِ اقْتُصِرَ عَلى إرادَتِهِ بِاللَّفْظِ. وادَّعى الجَلالُ المَحَلِّيُّ أنَّ المُلامَسَةَ حَقِيقَةٌ في الجَسِّ بِاليَدِ، مَجازٌ في الوَطْءِ، وأنَّ الشّافِعِيَّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ حَمَلَها عَلى المَعْنَيَيْنِ جَمْعًا بَيْنَ الحَقِيقَةِ والمَجازِ. وظاهِرُ عِبارَةِ (الأُمِّ) أنَّ الشّافِعِيَّ لَمْ يَحْمِلِ المُلامَسَةَ عَلى الوَطْءِ، بَلْ عَلى ما عَداهُ مِن أنْواعِ التِقاءِ البَشْرَتَيْنِ، وأنَّهُ إنَّما ذَكَرَ الجَسَّ بِاليَدِ تَمْثِيلًا لِلْمُلامَسَةِ بِنَوْعٍ مِن أنْواعِها، لا تَفْسِيرًا لَها بِذِكْرِ كَمالِ مَعْناها الحَقِيقِيِّ، كَما بَيَّنَهُ الكَمالُ ابْنُ أبِي شَرِيفٍ. فَلْيُفْهَمْ.

ثُمَّ إنَّ نَظْمَ هَذَيْنِ الأمْرَيْنِ في سِلْكِ سَبَبَيْ سُقُوطِ الطَّهارَةِ والمَصِيرِ إلى التَّيَمُّمِ، مَعَ كَوْنِهِما سَبَبَيْ وُجُوبِهِما، لَيْسَ بِاعْتِبارِ أنْفُسِهِما، بَلْ بِاعْتِبارِ قَيْدِهِما المُسْتَفادِ مِن قَوْلِهِ سُبْحانَهُ: ﴿فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا ماءً﴾، بَلْ هو السَّبَبُ في الحَقِيقَةِ، وإنَّما ذُكِرا تَمْهِيدًا لَهُ وتَنْبِيهًا عَلى أنَّهُ سَبَبٌ لِلرُّخْصَةِ بَعْدَ انْعِقادِ سَبَبِ الطَّهارَةِ بِقِسْمَيْها، كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: أوْ لَمْ تَكُونُوا مَرْضى أوْ مُسافِرِينَ، بَلْ كُنْتُمْ فاقِدِينَ لِلْماءِ بِسَبَبٍ مِنَ الأسْبابِ، مَعَ تَحَقُّقِ ما يُوجِبُ اسْتِعْمالَهُ مِنَ الحَدَثِ الأصْغَرِ أوِ الأكْبَرِ.

قِيلَ: وتَخْصِيصُ ذِكْرِهِ بِهَذِهِ الصُّورَةِ مَعَ أنَّهُ مُعْتَبَرٌ أيْضًا في صُورَةِ المَرَضِ والسَّفَرِ، لِنُدْرَةِ وُقُوعِهِ فِيها واسْتِغْنائِهِما عَنْ ذِكْرِهِ؛ لِأنَّ الجَنابَةَ مُعْتَبَرَةٌ فِيهِما قَطْعًا، فَيُعْلَمُ مِن حُكْمِها حُكْمُ الحَدَثِ الأصْغَرِ بِدَلالَةِ النَّصِّ؛ لِأنَّ تَقْدِيرَ النَّظْمِ: لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ في حالَةِ الجَنابَةِ إلّا كَوْنَكُمْ مُسافِرِينَ، فَإنْ كُنْتُمْ كَذَلِكَ أوْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى إلَخْ.

وقِيلَ: إنَّ هَذا القَيْدَ راجِعٌ لِلْكُلِّ، وقَيْدُ وُجُوبِ التَّطَهُّرِ المُكَنّى عَنْهُ بِالمَجِيءِ مِنَ الغائِطِ والمُلامَسَةِ مُعْتَبَرٌ فِيهِ أيْضًا. واعْتُرِضَ بِأنَّ النَّظْمَ الكَرِيمَ لا يُساعِدُهُ. وفي (الكَشْفِ) عَنْ بَعْضِهِمْ: أنَّ في الآيَةِ تَقْدِيمًا وتَأْخِيرًا، والتَّقْدِيرُ: ﴿لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وأنْتُمْ سُكارى ولا جُنُبًا﴾ ولا جائِيًا أحَدٌ مِنكم مِنَ الغائِطِ أوْ لامِسًا، يَعْنِي: ولا مُحْدِثِينَ، ثُمَّ قِيلَ: ﴿وإنْ كُنْتُمْ مَرْضى أوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ فَتَيَمَّمُوا﴾، وفِيهِ الفَصْلُ بَيْنَ الشَّرْطِ والجَزاءِ، والمَعْطُوفِ والمَعْطُوفِ عَلَيْهِ، مِن غَيْرِ نُكْتَةٍ. ثُمَّ قالَ بَعْدَ أنْ نَقَلَ ما اعْتَرَضَهُ: ولَعَلَّ الأوْجَهَ في تَقْرِيرِ الآيَةِ، واللَّهُ تَعالى أعْلَمُ، أنْ يُجْعَلَ عَدَمُ الوِجْدانِ عِبارَةً عَنْ عَدَمِ القُدْرَةِ عَلى اسْتِعْمالِ

[صفحة 43]

الماءِ لِفَقْدِ الماءِ أوْ لِمانِعٍ، لِيَصِحَّ أنْ يَكُونَ قَيْدًا لِلْكُلِّ، أوْ يُحْمَلَ عَلى ظاهِرِهِ ولا يُجْعَلَ قَيْدًا لِلْآخَرِينَ؛ لِأنَّ عُمُومَ الإعْوازِ في حَقِّ المُسافِرِ غالِبًا، والمَنعَ مِنَ القُدْرَةِ عَلى اسْتِعْمالِ الماءِ القائِمِ مَقامَهُ في حَقِّ المَرِيضِ مُغْنٍ عَنِ التَّقْيِيدِ لَفْظًا. وأنْ يَبْقى قَوْلُهُ سُبْحانَهُ: ﴿مَرْضى أوْ عَلى سَفَرٍ﴾ عَلى إطْلاقِهِ مِن غَيْرِ تَقْيِيدٍ بِكَوْنِهِمْ مُحْدِثِينَ أوْ مُجْنِبِينَ؛ لِأنَّ المَقْصُودَ بَيانُ سَبَبِ العُدُولِ عَنِ الطَّهارَةِ بِالماءِ إلى التَّيَمُّمِ، أمّا المُشْتَرَكُ بَيْنَ الطِّهارَتَيْنِ فَلا يُحْتاجُ إلى ذِكْرِهِ قَصْدًا. وأنْ يُجْعَلَ ذِكْرُ المُحْدِثِينَ مِن غَيْرِ القَبِيلَيْنِ بَيانًا لِسَبَبِ العُدُولِ، وهو فَقْدُ القُدْرَةِ مِن غَيْرِ سَفَرٍ ولا مَرَضٍ، لا لِأنَّ الحَدَثَ سَبَبٌ، وإنْ أفادَ ذَلِكَ ضِمْنًا.

ولَمْ يَقُلْ: "أوْ لَمْ تَجِدُوا" دُونَ ذِكْرِ السَّبَبَيْنِ، تَنْبِيهًا عَلى أنَّ عَدَمَ الوِجْدانِ مُرَخِّصٌ بَعْدَ انْعِقادِ سَبَبِ الطَّهارَةِ، وأُفِيدَ ضِمْنًا أنَّهُما مُعْتَبَرانِ أيْضًا في المَرِيضِ والمُسافِرِ، إذْ لا فَرْقَ بَيْنَ المَرَضِ والسَّفَرِ وبَيْنَ سائِرِ الأعْذارِ في ذَلِكَ. انْتَهى.

ولا يَخْفى أنَّ الحَمْلَ عَلى الظّاهِرِ أظْهَرُ، وما ذَكَرَهُ عَلى تَقْدِيرِ الحَمْلِ عَلَيْهِ لَيْسَ بِالبَعِيدِ عَمّا قَدَّمْناهُ. نَعَمِ، الآيَةُ مِن مُعْضِلاتِ القُرْآنِ، ولَعَلَّها تَحْتاجُ بَعْدُ إلى نَظَرٍ دَقِيقٍ.

والفاءُ في "فَلَمْ" عاطِفَةٌ. وأمّا الفاءُ في قَوْلِهِ سُبْحانَهُ: ﴿فَتَيَمَّمُوا صَعِيدًا طَيِّبًا﴾ فَواقِعَةٌ في جَوابِ الشَّرْطِ. والظّاهِرُ أنَّ الضَّمِيرَ راجِعٌ إلى جَمِيعِ ما اشْتَمَلَ عَلَيْهِ، وفِيهِ تَغْلِيبُ الخِطابِ عَلى الغَيْبَةِ، ومِثْلُهُ في ذَلِكَ "تَجِدُوا"، فَلا حاجَةَ إلى تَقْدِيرِ "فَلْيَتَيَمَّمْ" جَزاءً لِقَوْلِهِ سُبْحانَهُ: ﴿جاءَ أحَدٌ مِنكُمْ﴾.

والتَّيَمُّمُ لُغَةً: القَصْدُ، قالَ الأعْشى:

تَيَمَّمْتُ قَيْسًا وكَمْ دُونَهُ مِنَ الأرْضِ مِن مَهْمَهٍ ذِي شَزَنْ

*(I set my course for Qays, though between me and him lie many a desert expanse, desolate and rugged.)*

Al-Sa'id is the surface of the earth, as narrated from al-Khalil and Tha'lab. Al-Zajjaj said: "I know of no disagreement among the people of the language (ahl al-lughah) that al-sa'id is the surface of the earth. It was so named because it is the furthest point that is ascended to from the interior of the earth, or because of its rising and elevation above the earth." Al-tayyib is the pure, the clean. From Sufyan: the lawful (al-halal). It was also said: the place of growth, not the salt-flat, as in His, the Exalted, words: ﴿And the good land, its vegetation comes forth by the permission of its Lord﴾. Taking it in the first sense is the most fitting to the context of purity. The meaning is: intend and aim for something pure from the surface of the earth. This is clear evidence for the permissibility of tayammum with kohl, baked brick, marble (al-murdasanj), ruby (al-yaqut), turquoise (al-fayruzaj), coral (al-marjan), emerald (al-zumurrud), and the like, even if there is no dust upon it. This is the view of the Great Imam (al-Imam al-A'zam, Abu Hanifah) - may Allah be pleased with him - and Muhammad in one of the two narrations from him, and in another narration from him. It is the view of Abu Yusuf, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad - may Allah be pleased with them all - that tayammum is not permissible unless some dust clings to the hand, due to the restriction of the wiping by "from it" (minhu) in al-Ma'idah, and the particle "min" denotes partiality, and this requires dust. The Hanafis take it to mean the starting point (al-ibtida') or the emergence from the mostly-occurring sense. It was also said: the pronoun refers to the minor ritual impurity (hadath) understood from the context, and "min" is causal (lil-ta'lil).

Imam Malik was unusual in permitting tayammum with snow, and the Shi'ah have censured him for this. We have offered an explanation on his behalf in our book (al-Ajwibah al-Iraqiyyah 'an al-As'ilah al-Iraniyyah). "Sa'idan" is in the accusative as the object (maf'ul bihi). It was also said that it is accusative by the removal of the preposition, i.e. "fatayammamu bi-sa'id" (so perform tayammum with clean earth).

﴿So wipe your faces and your hands﴾, i.e. your faces and your hands, with the "ba'" being redundant (silah). The intended meaning is to cover these two limbs entirely with the wiping, so that if one leaves out any part of them it is not valid, as in wudu'. This is the apparent narration (zahir al-riwayah).

In a narration from al-Hasan from the Imam - may Allah be pleased with him - the majority of a part stands in place of the whole, because thoroughness (al-istay'ab) in what is wiped is not a condition, as in the wiping of the leather socks (khuff) and the head.

The apparent view is that tayammum stands in the place of wudu', and for this reason they said: one should pass the fingers through (yukhallil al-asabi') and remove the ring, in order to complete the wiping. Thoroughness in wudu' is a condition, so likewise in what takes its place. "Al-aydi" is the plural of "yad", and it is shared (mushtarakah) among several meanings: from the tips of the fingers to the wrist, to the elbow, and to the armpit.

صفحة 44

Is it literally (haqiqah) in one of these and metaphorical (majaz) in the others, or literally in all of them? Some have preferred the second, and for this reason some of the early generation (salaf) held each of these views. Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Zuhri that tayammum extends to the armpits.

He also narrated from Makhul that he said: "Tayammum is one strike for the face and the two palms down to the wrist (al-kuw')."

Al-Hakim narrated from Ibn 'Umar, concerning the manner of their tayammum with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "They wiped from the elbows to the palms, over the places of hair growth, from the outside and the inside." And from the hadith of Abu Dawud: "that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed tayammum and wiped his hands up to his elbows." This is our school and the school of al-Shafi'i and the majority. The analogy to wudu', of which it is the origin, supports them, even though the minor and major impurity (al-hadath wal-janabah) are equal in manner. Likewise, permissibility is also (established) according to the sound report narrated from the majority (al-mu'zam).

Among people there are those who say: the one in major impurity (junub), the menstruating woman (ha'id) and the woman in postnatal bleeding (nufasa') do not perform tayammum. This is narrated from 'Umar, his son, and Ibn Mas'ud - may Allah be pleased with them. It was said: the source of disagreement between them is whether the "mulamasah" mentioned earlier is taken to mean intercourse (al-wiqa') or touching with the hand. The earlier scholars took the first, and the later ones the latter. They said: analogically, tayammum should not be a means of purification; Allah the Exalted permitted it only for one in minor impurity, so it is not permitted for one in major impurity, because it is not of a rationally discernible meaning such that analogy would be valid, and major impurity is not in the same category as minor impurity so as to be joined to it, rather it is above it.

You know that the verse is, as it were, explicit in permitting tayammum for one in major impurity, even if "mulamasah" is not taken to mean intercourse, as its earlier explanation indicates. Moreover, the hadiths speak clearly to this. Al-Bukhari narrated from 'Imran ibn Husayn that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "saw a man standing apart who had not prayed with the people, and said: 'O so-and-so, what prevented you from praying?' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I have major impurity and there is no water.' He said: 'Upon you is the clean earth, for it will suffice you.'" It is also narrated that "some people came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: 'We are a people who live in these sands, and we have not found water for a month or two, and among us are the one in major impurity, the menstruating woman and the woman in postnatal bleeding?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Upon you is your land.'" And other than these. Whether tayammum lifts the minor impurity or not is a matter of disagreement, and the verse gives no indication of either position for one who considers it carefully.

﴿Indeed Allah is ever Pardoning, Forgiving﴾. This is a reason (ta'lil) for what the speech implies of concession and facilitation, and an affirmation of them, for whoever's constant custom is to pardon the erring and forgive the sinners must necessarily be one who facilitates, not one who burdens. It is permitted that it be a metonymy (kinayah) for that, for it is one of the concomitants (rawadif) of pardon and the followers (tawabi') of forgiveness. And it is incorporated into it that the basic principle is complete purity, and that other concessions are of the nature of pardon and forgiveness.

It was also said: "al-'afw" here means facilitation (al-taysir), as in "al-taysir," and its occurrence in this meaning is cited by the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "I have pardoned you the zakat on horses and slaves." Mentioning forgiveness is to indicate that He forgave the sin of those praying while intoxicated (sukara) and what occurred from them in recitation. You know that taking "al-'afw" as facilitation in the hadith is not necessary, and that the mention of forgiveness being related to what was mentioned is far-fetched.

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 4, verse 44:

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ This is a resumptive statement (istfa'naf) intended to make the believers marvel at their bad condition and to warn against allying with them, following the mention of the various kinds of obligations and legal rulings (al-taklif wa'l-ahkam al-shar'iyyah). The address is to everyone among the believers who is capable of seeing. It also serves as notice of the complete fame of the ugliness of their state. It has been said that it is addressed to the master of the addressees, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the address to the leader of a people is taken as an address to the people in his station. The verb "seeing" (ru'yah) is visual, and its transitivity with "ila" (to) is by treating it as meaning "looking" (al-nazar), i.e., "Have you not looked at them?" It may also be taken as cognitive, transitive with "ila" to imply the meaning of reaching (al-intiha'), i.e., "Has your knowledge not reached them, belittled in the station of amazement and of publicizing their shameful deeds, and placing them in the category of observable matters?"

The relative clause refers to the Jews of Madinah. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that it was revealed concerning Rifa'ah ibn Zayd and Malik ibn Dakhsham, who, whenever the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke, would twist their tongues and disparage him. And from him, it was revealed

صفحة 45

concerning two rabbis who used to come to 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his group, discouraging them from Islam.

"The Book" refers to the Torah. It has been said that it is the genus, and [those Jews] enter into it by primary entry, and there is in this a lengthening of the distance. It has been said that it is the Qur'an, because the Jews knew that it is a true Book, brought by a truthful Prophet, with no doubt about his prophethood, but this is contrary to the apparent meaning.

"With what they were given" (bi'l-ladhi uwtuhu) refers to what was made clear to them in it of rulings and knowledge, among which is what they knew of the description of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The expression of it as "portion" (nasib) implies that it is a right of theirs which must be observed and preserved, to indicate the feebleness of their opinions in neglecting it. The indefinite form (al-tanwin) is for magnification, and it supports the censure; the same applies if it is taken to mean abundance. "Min" (from) is connected to an omitted element that functions as an adjective of "nasiban," clarifying its relational magnificence following its intrinsic magnificence. It has also been said that it is connected to "uwtu" (were given).

The statement of the Exalted, ﴿they purchase error﴾, is a resumptive statement clarifying the basis of the censure and the focus of the amazement that were understood from the beginning of the speech. It is built on a question arising from it, as if it were said: "What do they do such that he looks at them?" So it was said: they choose error over guidance, or they exchange it for it after having possessed it, treated as attained, or its attainment for them is actual through their denial of the prophethood of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that they take bribes and distort the Torah, so the error is this distortion, i.e., they bought it with the wealth of bribery. Abu'l-Baqa' held that the clause "they purchase" is a presumed circumstantial clause (hal muqaddarah) from the pronoun of "uwtu," or a circumstantial clause from "alladhina." The first view was objected to on the grounds that considering their purchase as mentioned within the giving is certainly not fitting for the context, and the second on the grounds that it fails to convey that the matter of censure and amazement is the mentioned purchase and what is conjoined to it, the Exalted's statement: ﴿and they want you to lose the way﴾.

Therefore the more preferable view is resumption, and the conjoined element is a partner of the element it is conjoined to in what preceded it. The meaning is that they are not content with their own misguidance, but by what they have done of denying the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and concealing his descriptions that the Torah speaks of, they want you also to be misguided from the straight path that leads to the truth. The use of the present tense in both places indicates continuous renewal; so the ruling of their mentioned purchasing is renewed, and the repeated practice according to its requirement is in the sense of its own renewal and repetition. In this too is a degree of censure that is not hidden.

It is read: ﴿an yadillu﴾ with the ya', with the dad fatha and kasra.

Al-Alusi, *Ruh al-Ma'ani*, on surah 4, verse 45:

﴿And Allah knows best﴾ [about] your enemies, O believers, ﴿your enemies﴾, those who are among them, these [people]. He has already informed you of their enmity toward you and of what they intend, so beware of them. The sentence is *mu'taridah* (an interjected clause, inserted parenthetically) for emphasis and for explaining the warning. Otherwise, Allah's knowing is already known. It has also been said that the meaning is that He, exalted is He, knows their condition and the outcome of their affair, so do not turn toward them, and do not be preoccupied with thinking about them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a protector﴾, who takes charge of your affairs and benefits you as He wills. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a helper﴾, who repels from you their scheming and their evil. So be content with His guardianship and His support, do not concern yourselves with them, and do not be in distress over what they plot. This contains a promise to the believers and a threat to their enemies. This sentence is also parenthetical. The *ba'* is superfluous (*zā'idah*) in the subject of *kafā* (sufficed), for emphasis on the attribution, with what conveys attachment, namely the *ba' al-ilsāq* (the *ba'* of attachment).

Al-Zajjaj said: This *ba'* entered only because the sense of the speech is: "Be content with Allah." And *waliyyan* and *nasiran* are in the accusative of specification (*tamyīz*). It has also been said that they are in the circumstantial accusative (*hāl*). The repetition of the verb in both clauses, together with the explicit mention of the glorious Name, serves to emphasize His sufficiency, may He be glorified and exalted, while also indicating the causal connection.

[p. 46]

**"Among those who are Jews"** (﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾). It has been said that this is a clarification of **"those who were given"** (﴿لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا﴾), which is understood in meaning as referring to the People of the Two Books. Something has been placed between the two phrases in order to give greater attention to clarifying the object of censure and wonder, to hasten the warning of the believers against them, and to encourage them to rely on Allah, the Exalted, and to be satisfied with His protection and His support.

Abu Hayyan objected to this, saying: al-Farisi (d. 377 AH) prohibited an interjected clause (i'tiraḍ) with two sentences, so what do you think about three? Al-Halabi answered that the prohibition applies when there is no conjunction, and here the sentences are conjoined, and through the conjunction the two become one thing.

It has also been said that it is a clarification of **"your enemies"** (﴿أَعْدائِكُمْ﴾). But in this there is the problem that there is no reason to single out His knowledge, glory be to Him, as regarding a group of their enemies, especially in the context of an interjection.

It has also been said that it is a relative complement (ṣila) of **"a helper"** (﴿نَصِيرٍ﴾), meaning: "He will help you (﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾)." But in this there is a restriction on the broad scope of Allah the Exalted's help, and there is no need to place a relative pronoun in the position of the pronoun referring to the enemies. Moreover, that what falls within the relative clause is a description suitable for help is not apparent.

It has also been said that it is the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada'), and His saying, the Exalted: **"They distort the words from their places"** (﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ الكَلِمَ عَنْ مَواضِعِهِ﴾), is a descriptive phrase (ṣifa) for it, meaning: "Among those who are Jews is a people who distort." This is required in the reading of Abdullah, and it is established that when the subject is described by a clause or an adverbial phrase, and it is a part of an indefinite noun governed by **min** (from), or is in a position preceding it, its omission is regular. Among examples of this is the verse:

*"And time is nothing but two turns: in one of them I die, and in the other I strive, seeking life."*

Al-Farra' takes the omitted subject to be a relative pronoun (ism mawṣūl), and **"they distort"** (﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ﴾) its relative clause, meaning: "Among those who are Jews are those who distort." The Basrans prohibit omitting the relative pronoun while retaining its relative clause. However, what supports this is what is in the Codex of Hafsa, may Allah be pleased with her: **"those who distort"** (﴿مَن يُحَرِّفُونَ﴾).

This too has been objected to, on the grounds that by its apparent meaning it entails that the preceding group is far removed from distortion, which is the reality of their purchasing (of error).

**"The word"** (**al-kalim**, الكَلِمُ) is a collective noun (ism jins), its singular being **kalima**, like **libina** and **libin**, and **nabiqa** and **nabiq**. It has also been said that it is a plural, but this is not among the preferred views. Perhaps the one who applied it to this meant the linguistic sense, namely what indicates more than two in general. The pronoun referring to it is masculine in view of its individual units in form, and plural in view of its multiplicity in meaning.

It was read with a kasra on the kaf and sukun on the lam, as the plural of **kilma** (کِلْمَة), a lightened form of **kalima**, by transferring the kasra of the lam to the kaf. It was also read **"they distort the speech"** (**al-kalam**). The intended meaning here is either what is in the Torah, or what is more general than that, including the words that will be related of them later, which they uttered during their dialogue with the Messenger (ﷺ). The first is what is transmitted from the early generations (salaf), such as Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and others.

The distortion of that is either its removal from the places where Allah the Exalted placed it in the Torah, like their distortion of **"of medium build"** (**rab'a**) in the description of the Prophet (ﷺ), and their putting **"tall"** (**ṭiwāl**) in its place; and like their distortion of stoning (al-rajm) by putting the prescribed punishment (al-ḥadd) in its place. Or it is turning it away from the meaning that Allah the Exalted sent down in it toward what has no validity, through corrupt interpretations and deviant contrivances, as the innovators (mubtadi'a) do with the Qur'anic verses that oppose their school.

The first view is supported by what al-Bukhari related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "How do you ask the People of the Book about anything, when your Book, which was sent down to His Messenger, is more recent? You recite it pure, unmixed. He has told you that the People of the Book altered the Book of Allah, the Exalted, changed it, and wrote the Book with their own hands, and said: 'This is from Allah,' so that they might purchase with it a small price." It was objected: how is that possible for a Book whose individual letters and words have reached the level of mass transmission (tawātur), and whose copies have spread east and west?

It was answered that this happened before the Book became famous throughout the regions and reached the level of mass transmission. But this is far-fetched, even though it is supported by the occurrence of variation among the copies of the Torah held by the various Jewish sects.

It has been said that the Jews did this in some copies of the Torah in order to mislead people with them. When this did not succeed, they turned to interpretation. The meaning of **"its places"** (﴿مَواضِعِهِ﴾), if the more general meaning is intended, is whatever is fitting for it in every respect, whether that is by its specification by Allah the Exalted explicitly, as with the places of what is in the Torah, or by the specification of reason and religion, as with the places of other things.

The root meaning of **tahrīf** (distortion) is inclining a thing toward a side (ḥarf), that is, an edge. So if **"they distort"** (**yuḥarrifūna**) means "they remove," it is a metaphor (kināya), because when they replace the word and put something else in its place, it necessarily follows that they have inclined it away from its places and distorted it.

The difference between this passage and what comes in Surat al-Ma'ida in His saying, glory be to Him: **"after its places"** (﴿مِن بَعْدِ مَواضِعِهِ﴾), is that the latter is more indicative of the established firmness of the places of the words and their fame than this one. That is because the adverbial phrase indicates that they distorted the word after the place had been established and settled. The former was chosen there, because there is something that calls for the more indicative and more eloquent expression.

**"And they say"** (﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾) is coordinated with **"they distort"** (﴿يُحَرِّفُونَ﴾). Most scholars hold that what is meant by it is verbal speech in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ). Some chose to interpret it as covering that and whatever their stubbornness and obstinacy translate into, so that what the tongues of their state spoke when they distorted the Torah is included in it. It is then not restricted to a time or place, nor specified to one matter rather than another. This requires the employment of a general metaphor, so that the combination of literal and metaphorical meaning is avoided. The meaning according to this is that, along with that distortion, they say and understand, in every matter that opposes their corrupt desires, whether it is in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), or by the tongue of the state, or of speech, out of obstinacy and to make their opposition real.

**"We hear"** (﴿سَمِعْنا﴾), that is: we understood. **"And we disobey"** (﴿وَعَصَيْنا﴾), that is: we did not obey. al-Raghib (d. 502 AH) explained it this way.

**"And hear, without being heard"** (﴿وَاسْمَعْ غَيْرَ مُسْمَعٍ﴾) is coordinated with **"we hear"** (﴿سَمِعْنا﴾), included with it under "say," but considering that it is verbal. It is said during their address to the Prophet (ﷺ). It is a statement with two faces, admitting both evil and good, and in rhetoric (badī') this is called **tawjīh** (double-directed phrasing), as many have said. They illustrated it with the verse:

*"Amr sewed me a qaba' (robe), would that his two eyes were level!"*

Its admitting of evil is that it may be understood as: "Hear!" invoking a curse on you, "may you not hear!"; or "Hear" as one not responding to what you call for; or "Hear" as one deaf to what he hears, out of dislike toward you; or "Hear" a speech that does not reach you ("without being heard") because your ears recoil from it. So **ghayra** (غَيْرَ) is either a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl) not a direct object, or it is an object. The circumstantial reading is valid under the first possibility, because the supplication is what they intend, and since they, may Allah curse them, estimated its answer, it became as though it were an established, fixed fact.

Its admitting of good is that it may be understood as: "Hear from us," "unheard" of what is disliked, from the expression **asma'ahu fulān** when someone reviles him, whose original form was "ushmi'uhu mā yakrah" (I make him hear what he dislikes). Its object was omitted, being forgotten and neglected, and this became customary in that usage. They, may Allah curse them, used to address the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with it mockingly, showing him the latter meaning while concealing another.

**"And ra'ina"** (﴿وَراعِنا﴾) is coordinated with what precedes it, meaning: they also say this in the course of addressing him (ﷺ). It has two faces like the preceding one.
